report.source_text: MRI of the brain (figure 1) was done, which revealed a thick-walled peripherally enhancing lesion of size ~45×43×37 mm in the right parietal lobe in the peritrigonal location. The lesion wall had crenulated margins with intracavitary projections, which showed blooming on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) and diffusion restriction on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). The core of the lesion was hyperintense, which was suppressed on a fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequence. Marked perilesional oedema was also seen on T2-weighted/FLAIR imaging with surrounding mass effect. On magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), raised lipid lactates and trehalose were seen.

clinician.final_diagnosis: the formation of fungal brain abscess following COVID-19 ... Aspergillus ... The culture of the pus had grown Aspergillus organism.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 62-year-old man, recently discharged post-COVID-19 pneumonia, presented with altered behavior, slurring of speech, and left-side weakness. MRI of the brain revealed a thick-walled, peripherally enhancing lesion in the right parietal lobe consistent with an abscess, with MRS findings suggestive of fungal infection. A craniotomy with excision of the brain abscess was performed, and culture of the pus grew Aspergillus organism. CT of the thorax showed peripheral pulmonary cavities, segmental right pulmonary artery thrombus, and diffuse parenchymal fibrosis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with neurological symptoms (altered behavior, slurring of speech, left-side weakness) after recent COVID-19 pneumonia hospitalization.

MRI brain showed a thick-walled, peripherally enhancing lesion in the right parietal lobe, consistent with an abscess, with features like crenulated margins, intracavitary projections, blooming on SWI, diffusion restriction on DWI, perilesional edema, and mass effect.
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) showed raised lipid lactates and trehalose, indicative of fungal infection.
Craniotomy with excision of the brain abscess was performed.
Culture of the pus from the excised lesion grew Aspergillus organism, confirming the fungal etiology.
CT of the thorax showed peripheral pulmonary cavities, segmental right pulmonary artery thrombus, and diffuse parenchymal fibrosis, suggesting potential pulmonary involvement or source.

remaining_uncertainties: Patient's detailed clinical response to treatment
